title: Generate the closed set of state-handle registration and receipt adapters once
evidence: state.rs repeats the same six-domain construction and domain-name/error association across ordinary registration, schema-validation registration, reacquisition and recovery-candidate acquisition (roughly 230 lines). The individual domain facades repeat register/reacquire/revision/committed_revision forwarding with the same type-specific handle relationship.

Ordinary bootstrap registers the session first and deliberately defers dormant-domain exhaustive validation. Candidate acquisition binds the recovery generation. These are semantic modes, so a blanket constructor that changes mode/order would be incorrect.
Runtime-root, settings and durable-job listing paths repeatedly reconstruct StatePage from the same home-store page metadata.
proposal: Use one private declarative inventory for the fixed domain handles, expanding the existing typed facade adapters and the repeated BerylState construction. Keep explicit ordinary/schema-validation/candidate entry points, bootstrap ordering, domain names and attachment behavior. A small StatePage conversion can remove repeated metadata forwarding. Estimated net removal 180–260 lines after the macro and adapters; avoid a public dynamic domain registry.
required_contract_changes: No public type, bootstrap timing, validation boundary, receipt authority or recovery-generation change. Internal implementation description may mention the fixed inventory.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Preserve existing reopen_validation, recovery and commit_receipts scenarios, including ordinary reopen deferral and rejection of prior-generation handles/receipts. Review macro expansion for every domain and acquisition mode.

title: Use thiserror for conventional state errors while preserving error-source topology
evidence: Manual Display/Error/From implementations recur throughout all six domains and theme services. Representative bodies: state.rs:392-463; runtime_root/error.rs:41-166; session/error.rs:128-286; durable_job.rs:400-547; catalog.rs:409-620; asset/error.rs:231-369; theme/manifest.rs:710-867.

Many wrappers expose Some(inner) through Error::source while displaying the inner message. #[error(transparent)] can skip that wrapper layer. AssetMutationError and several theme errors currently implement empty Error despite carrying other errors. A field named source is inferred by thiserror even without explicit attributes.
Root Cargo.toml already selects thiserror 2.0.18. Shared exact-version investigation is retained in doc/memory/crates.io/thiserror/2.0.18/manual-error-simplification.md.
proposal: Add the existing workspace thiserror dependency to beryl-state. Derive conventional error formatting and sources with exact messages and explicit per-variant source decisions. Preserve DomainCallbackError classification manually. Retain manual Error/From implementations where a derive would expose a hidden cause; do not force opaque readiness errors into a different public representation. Estimated net removal 600–900 lines excluding error code deleted by ST-003 or the optional ST-014 parser replacement.
required_contract_changes: None if enum shape, messages, source chains and conversions remain identical. Any intentional source-topology change is a separate API decision, not a simplification assumption.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Compare every variant's Display and complete source chain, especially wrapper-versus-transparent and inferred fields named source/backtrace. Keep direct-read versus semantic DomainCallbackError provenance tests.
Member-manifest implementation requires locked metadata validation and focused Cargo check before analyzer restart; then existing focused state nextest coverage.

required_contract_changes: None for durable formats or public typed errors. If a new common codec error variant is exposed, document that API change explicitly; prefer adapters preserving existing categories.

assets_v3.rs:219-280 accepts content_id_byte/content_digest_byte but discards both at line 238; digest.rs changes only an ignored parameter for its content-neutrality equality assertion. That comparison exercises identical effective inputs.

Estimated net removal 650–1,050 lines after helpers; no blanket deletion of cross-layer tests.

title: Represent the closed durable-job transition family with one mutation implementation
evidence: durable_job/mutation/transition.rs contains 505 lines for seven related transition structs and DomainMutation implementations. Each reads one JobRecordV1, checks expected revision/lifecycle, advances the record, reserves one job plus one live-index slot and publishes the job with a live-index put/delete.

The differing transition predicates and updates are a closed finite match. The authoritative failure compatibility matrix in record.rs:265-301 also governs decode validation; admission is a different five-family closure and must remain separate.
proposal: Use a private closed transition enum carrying variant-specific payloads and one DomainMutation implementation for common read/revision/reservation/contribution mechanics. Preserve existing typed constructors/facade methods as concise factories. Keep each lifecycle/failure predicate explicit in the match and preserve terminal index deletion. Estimated net removal 200–260 lines after the enum and factories.
required_contract_changes: No lifecycle, retry policy, command footprint, durable version or public constructor change. Any consolidation of the public API would be a separate contract proposal.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Run durable_job, failure-compatibility, failure-corruption and concurrency-domain tests; preserve all legal/illegal stage-failure pairs, stale revisions, retry attempt identity, live index and reopen evidence.

title: Share exhaustive cursor-loop mechanics while keeping domain invariants explicit
evidence: runtime_root/validate.rs:149-238 already centralizes typed full-range scans. Asset validation has its own range helper, while durable-job validation repeats five paginated loops and catalog validation repeats two.

The repeated pieces are range initialization, page request, empty-with-has_more rejection and exclusive continuation. Each domain still owns cross-index equality, carry state, bounded limits and its semantic error variant.

Session bootstrap/acquisition deliberately performs one bounded page with fixed window/claim budgets; window acquisition's catalog scan carries cancellation, repair precedence and one retained match. Those are not instances to absorb into a universal scan.
proposal: Introduce or reuse one private visitor helper for explicit lower/upper bounds, page limits and continuation, with a narrow error adapter. Keep each invariant visitor and its cross-page carry state local. Do not collect a whole domain or merge ordinary reads with exhaustive scrub. Estimated net removal 100–180 lines after generic bounds and adapters; abandon the abstraction if those costs erase the reduction.
required_contract_changes: None for ordinary-versus-exhaustive validation, page limits, record ordering, cancellation or typed corruption provenance.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Existing explicit scrub/reopen corruption coverage plus multi-page boundary cases for missing index copies, cross-page owner/job carry state and empty continuation; ensure no whole-domain collection is introduced.

title: Remove duplicated catalog row validation and unnecessary deep row copies
evidence: catalog/acquisition.rs:140-190 validates a page and clones each row for comparison and again into its output while the original page remains live; current_row_source compares against Some(row.clone()).

catalog/mutation.rs:212-250 and :275-305 repeat claimed-row, selection, runtime/root and exact-current checks. Release rejects initial rows while delete requires them; that origin distinction is exercised by window_abandonment tests.
proposal: Consume page rows into the checked result and compare borrowed row values. Extract the shared exact claimed-row checks into one private helper with explicit origin requirements, retaining release-versus-delete publication. Estimated net removal 35–60 lines, with fewer bounded but potentially large row copies.
required_contract_changes: None; preserve stale-row repair/error precedence, exact recency copy checks and created-versus-reused origin rejection.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.
Existing catalog corruption/page/claim tests and window_abandonment cross-origin, retained-index and unrelated-progress tests; check exact output order and page metadata.

title: Retain exact Unicode 17 NFKC_Casefold until a replacement proves the full mapping contract
evidence: catalog/normalization.rs consumes a 160,384-byte generated Unicode 17 mapping table (10,583 mappings and 8,343 mapped values), then uses pinned unicode-normalization 0.1.25 for NFC. The table generator reads NFKC_CF from DerivedNormalizationProps rather than a generic lowercase/casefold table.

Unicode default ignorables, compatibility mappings, expansion ordering, canonical composition and exact version pinning affect durable normalized-title bytes. Existing tests exercise soft hyphen, combining sequences, expansions and a pinned table digest.

Official icu_normalizer 2.3.0 ComposingNormalizer documentation exposes NFC/NFKC constructors; ICU4X CaseMapper is a separate component. Combining those APIs is not evidence that Beryl's exact Unicode 17 R5 transformation is preserved.
proposal: Retain the custom mapping table, generator and pinned NFC dependency in this audit. A future ICU4X adapter must prove exact Unicode-version data, default-ignorable removal, full casefold ordering and bounded expansion against the entire pinned UCD corpus before a replacement can be priced. Generic case-insensitive equality, lowercase or NFKC alone is not an accepted substitute. No line-saving claim is included.
required_contract_changes: None for retention. Changing normalized bytes or Unicode revision would be a persisted catalog-format/semantic change and must be explicitly designed rather than hidden in a dependency swap.
verification: No builds or corpus comparisons executed. Existing Unicode golden cases and table-digest assertions remain required.
Any later replacement needs exhaustive per-code-point NFKC_CF comparison plus interacting multi-code-point normalization sequences and catalog encode/decode compatibility.

dependency_candidates.features: Normalizer defaults compiled_data, utf8_iter and utf16_iter; compiled_data includes matching baked data. A proposed adapter would need exact coordinated component/data versions.
dependency_candidates.platform: Pure Rust, workspace MSRV 1.88 below Beryl 1.92; no native ICU install needed for ICU4X.
dependency_candidates.semantic_gaps: No direct NFKC_Casefold constructor in reviewed ComposingNormalizer API; combined normalizer/casemap/property semantics and precise Unicode 17 data not proved. Dependency closure/advisories not qualified; no safety clearance claimed.

title: Share the theme lexical primitives under the existing streaming contract
evidence: theme/document.rs:569-687,888-909 and theme/manifest.rs:458-484,563-669 each implement comment/quoted-string/escape mechanics.

The accepted subsets differ: documents support basic and literal strings plus typed role values and InstalledLoad omission; manifest strings use a stricter subset, and the two writers differ in which Unicode controls they escape. The document and manifest line/CRLF byte-accounting limits also differ.
Current system authority requires incremental parsing and package authority forbids whole-document residency; local lexical reuse can satisfy both.
proposal: Share only equivalent basic-string escape decoding and small lexical mechanics, with explicit mode arguments for supported quote forms/control handling where needed. Keep field admission, installed omission, duplicate detection, canonical output ordering and line/page budgets local. Estimated net removal 70–110 lines after adapters. Prefer this low-risk local option when the whole-document alternative ST-014 is not selected; do not add both alternatives' savings.
required_contract_changes: None if existing syntax and canonical bytes are preserved. Unifying previously different admitted syntax or escaping is an explicit theme-format decision.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Existing document and physical-manifest tests, plus focused equivalence at escaped quotes/backslashes, literal quotes, Unicode escapes and controls, trailing comments, CRLF limit edges, installed unknown values and duplicate entries. Preserve typed limits and exact digest identity.

Factor common prepared manifest-change metadata and checked physical-decoder construction. Retain the two-pass hash-then-stream physical API, command-specific guards and immediate pre-publication freshness/reference checks. Estimated net removal 150–240 lines after context/helper types; no global execution framework.

Existing theme_execution/physical_service tests for all repository operations, 1,024 entries, 1 MiB manifest, smaller source caps, no-stage refusal, SaveAs binding, concurrent physical replacement and exact old/new/collision reconciliation.

title: Replace theme reconciliation's temporary optional payloads with complete internal outcomes
evidence: ThemeIndeterminateOperation at execution.rs:52-57 temporarily carries evidence: Some and expected: Some. register_outcome:370-411 takes both, installs a complete RetainedOperation and constructs a second boxed operation with both fields None. Public callers only observe operation().

ThemeNaturalRepositoryIdentity::checked at command.rs:473-492 validates an allocated document Vec then retains only the manifest. ThemeReconciliationDescriptor validates old/new homes/generations then retains only operation. expected_publication allocates/duplicates those wrappers; map_mutation_outcome constructs the descriptor after an indeterminate physical mutation.

Serena references show natural-identity/descriptor use is private to theme execution and its crate-private re-export. The public indeterminate type is produced only by the two internal outcome mappers, so its opaque operation identity can remain unchanged.
proposal: Use a complete private pending outcome containing operation/evidence/expected, and expose the existing public operation handle only after ownership is registered. Consolidate expected-publication validation into one checked constructor before physical mutation, storing old manifest, publication and operation without disposable document vectors/wrappers. Preserve service-scoped retention, exact comparison and collision gates. Estimated net removal 80–130 lines beyond ST-012; keep any necessary validation rather than merely deleting it.
required_contract_changes: No public outcome or operation-id semantics need change because fields are private. Move validation before side effects without weakening accepted old/new identity relations.
verification: Audit only; no tests/builds executed.

Existing theme exact-old/exact-new/collision tests, dropped public handle, independent service versus shared clone ownership, registry release and unknown-operation rejection. Review every indeterminate path to ensure custody enters the registry once and cannot be lost.

title: Replace the theme-document parser with existing TOML deserialization after explicitly allowing capped whole-document parsing
evidence: theme/document.rs is 909 lines and owns hand-written line/assignment/string/numeric parsing alongside semantic role admission and canonical output. The newly fixed 256 KiB document ceiling creates a concrete bounded whole-input alternative.

doc/systems/theme-runtime/design.md:75-78 currently mandates an incremental parser with no whole-document alternate path; crates/beryl-state/doc/design-theme-settings.md:39-42 says no read requires a whole document resident. This proposal therefore changes authority rather than claiming the existing TOML crate is a drop-in fit.

Exact workspace-resolved toml is 0.9.12+spec-1.1.0. Its tagged parser materializes tokens, events and a DeTable before serde conversion and retains an 80-level recursion guard unless unbounded is enabled. An input-byte ceiling is not an exact heap ceiling.

The tagged ValueDeserializer can visit u64/u128; toml::Value::Integer is i64. Direct typed deserialization preserves full-width numeric fields better than a generic Value intermediate. The library supports TOML 1.1 syntax beyond the current compact subset, and malformed unknown InstalledLoad fields currently may be skipped before value parsing.
proposal: Choose one parser for all theme-document entry points: read through a cap+1 bounded reader, validate UTF-8 and existing line/property/role bounds, deserialize bounded raw theme records with the existing toml/serde dependencies, then apply the existing semantic validator and mode-specific unknown-field policy. Preserve exact file length/digest observations and final physical freshness checks. Keep manifest streaming/paging and the physical publication protocol unchanged. Decide admitted TOML grammar explicitly and retain canonical serialization if byte compatibility is required. Estimated net removal 350–550 lines including raw DTOs, error adapters and bound checks. This is an alternative to ST-011, not additive savings; prototype allocation/diagnostic fit before implementation planning.
required_contract_changes: Change theme-runtime and package authority to allow one 256 KiB capped whole-document parse, with a documented temporary dependency allocation limitation and bounded concurrent parser count. Preserve existing feature size/role/property limits.

Specify whether standard TOML 1.1 syntax becomes accepted and whether malformed unknown InstalledLoad values now fail syntax validation. Either decision must be visible in the supported theme-format contract; do not silently narrow installed-load behavior.

Update exact parser-error classification/line diagnostics only through an explicit contract decision. Reconcile the bounded-resource rule on whole-value dependencies at this fixed document boundary; no allowance for whole manifest, draft, transcript or catalog residency is proposed.
verification: Audit only; no prototype, builds or tests executed.

Before adopting: compare current syntax/mode corpus against the proposed parser, including duplicate roles/properties, unknown malformed values, literal/basic strings, nonfinite/numeric bounds, Unicode escapes, CRLF line limits and canonical output.

Measure allocation/latency at 256 KiB with many tiny tokens and nested unknown values while the default recursion guard is enabled; set and exercise a finite concurrency envelope. Preserve physical race rejection and all existing theme document/semantic tests.
